body:
https://secure.ngpvan.com/2_h6cpffIkGCBPjTjtmFVw2?contactdata=z+OW0Hqcyk8zcIYi0FI0H7osMAtfRhTte0t7gMRuJSbsgoFPy5LlSNqunWx+TwQAgV7b1VGKRLFmCPVMZqXR4wOXI+9xIsB3SzFhY8lUF4OgROhqqBLnK3bgXEtxJn98 [https://secure.ngpvan.com/2_h6cpffIkGCBPjTjtmFVw2?contactdata=z+OW0Hqcyk8zcIYi0FI0H7osMAtfRhTte0t7gMRuJSbsgoFPy5LlSNqunWx+TwQAgV7b1VGKRLFmCPVMZqXR4wOXI+9xIsB3SzFhY8lUF4OgROhqqBLnK3bgXEtxJn98]
Hi Peter,
As of today, the League of Conservation Voters (LCV) launched the 2025 National Environmental Scorecard! Check the scores of your Congress members and senators here. [http://lcv.org/scorecard]
The 2025 National Environmental Scorecard highlights our state’s leaders and their work to protect our environment despite an unprecedented year with a record number of attacks on our environment and democracy. The 2025 Scorecard [http://lcv.org/2025-scorecard] exemplifies the stark contrast between Democrats and Republicans in Congress. The majority of our delegation fought against Republicans in Congress who repeatedly chose loyalty to the Trump administration and Big Polluters over making life more affordable, safer, and healthier for their own constituents. The result has been higher energy costs for working families, lost jobs and economic opportunities, the sell-off of tens of millions of acres of public lands and waters to Big Polluters, fewer clean air and water safeguards, and increased pollution. Congressional Republicans threatened free and fair elections; however, thanks to Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley these efforts were blocked in the Senate.
Oregon’s U.S. Senators both received high scores: Ron Wyden with a perfect 100% score, and Jeff Merkley with a high 97%. Join us in thanking Senators Wyden and Merkley for their commitment to standing up for our climate! [https://secure.ngpvan.com/2_h6cpffIkGCBPjTjtmFVw2]
This year, many in our state’s delegation led efforts to help local communities lower costs, tackle the climate crisis, protect public lands, and stand up to Trump’s attacks. But a Trump-led agenda in Congress made efforts for progress impossible.
Oregon’s U.S. Representatives Bonamici, Dexter, and Salinas all received perfect scores of 100%! We want to thank U.S. Representative Hoyle for earning 97%, and U.S Representative Bynum for earning 91%. Join us in celebrating some of our U.S. Representatives by thanking them for being a climate champ! [https://secure.ngpvan.com/2_h6cpffIkGCBPjTjtmFVw2]
Send your messages! [https://secure.ngpvan.com/2_h6cpffIkGCBPjTjtmFVw2?contactdata=z+OW0Hqcyk8zcIYi0FI0H7osMAtfRhTte0t7gMRuJSbsgoFPy5LlSNqunWx+TwQAgV7b1VGKRLFmCPVMZqXR4wOXI+9xIsB3SzFhY8lUF4OgROhqqBLnK3bgXEtxJn98]
We’re grateful to have so many pro-environment members of Congress working for our state. However, we do want to mention that U.S. Representative Bentz earned an embarrassing 3% score. It’s time for Representative Bentz to step up for our climate. Take a moment and tell him to do better by sending him a message here. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/2_h6cpffIkGCBPjTjtmFVw2]
Make sure you check out LCV’s full 2025 Environmental Scorecard here [http://lcv.org/scorecard] , and join us in celebrating our climate champs right here in Oregon and asking Representative Bentz to step up!
Thank you for being a part of our community!
Sincerely,
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVLCV/1/70877/images/Britney_signature-removebg-preview.png]
Britney VanCitters (she/her)

Friends,Wisconsin comedian Charlie Berens recently joked that _“we have more regulations on a bratwurst than the entire artificial intelligence community.”_ It’s funny but it raises some real questions.Wisconsin is seeing proposals for massive new data centers that will likely permanently shape our communities. They can bring jobs and investment, and I’m not against public support for growth when it makes sense.But when projects are this large, Wisconsin families deserve one simple guarantee:**No hidden costs.** Families and small businesses shouldn’t end up paying indirectly, whether through utility rates, infrastructure strain, or long-term taxpayer risk that wasn’t clear from the start.We’ve learned from recent large developments, like Foxconn, that they work best when expectations are honest and transparent from day one. Growth should strengthen communities, not create surprises later. That means leaders doing their job, protecting taxpayers with clear agreements, accountability, and clawbacks if promises aren't kept. That’s the balance I’ll continue to advocate for.I’d like to hear your thoughts on this — just hit reply and let me know.Conversations like this are how we build better policy and a stronger Wisconsin.
\- Mike

subject: My exchange with the President →
body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20260226-1972-foote&t=1001&akid=1972%2E342411%2EJcgRF3 ]Squad Victory Fund

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20260226-movement.GDMDGj&refcode=em20260226-1972&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=1972%2E342411%2EJcgRF3 ]Tweet from CSPAN: President Trump: 'You should be ashamed of yourself.'
Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN): 'You have killed Americans.'

Peter, I got into
it with the President two nights ago.

I’m not going to stay silent while the most powerful man lies about my
community and spreads even more fear and hatred.

The truth is simple: Donald Trump has killed innocent Americans. Two of
them were my constituents. Their names are Alex Pretti and Renee Good.

But those names did not come out of the President's mouth. Because he is a
coward.

Trump should be ashamed of himself — him and the entire Republican Party
have no empathy for their fellow Americans. They don’t care that ICE
murdered two citizens in cold-blood; that’s just collateral damage to them
as they pursue their violent agenda of brutal crackdowns, mass detention,
and deportation.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20260226-movement.GDMDGj&refcode=em20260226-1972&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1003&akid=1972%2E342411%2EJcgRF3 ]If you’re with me in the fight to defeat these cowardly fascists and
turn back the clock on their destructive agenda, please rush a
contribution to the Squad Victory Fund to power our movement today >>

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20260226-movement.GDMDGj&refcode=em20260226-1972&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1004&akid=1972%2E342411%2EJcgRF3 ]RUSH A DONATION

I spoke up with fire in my heart. Because I’m angry as hell.

ICE swooped into my community based on a lie; that the Somali-American
community is collectively guilty for the actions of a small few. That the
very existence of people who look like me and share my story are not
acceptable in Trump’s America.

They used this lie to unleash absolute chaos.

ICE agents all but suspended civil rights in their pursuit of
deportations. Anyone with an accent or a different skin color was stopped
in the street or in their cars and racially profiled. Homes were violently
entered without proper warrants. Everyone from refugees to legal residents
to US citizens were swept up in illegal detentions.

When protesters and observers mobilized to fight back, ICE responded with
unprecedented brutality. Ramming into civilian cars. Beating protesters
with steel batons. Throwing innocent people to the ground. Ripping people
from their vehicles through shattered glass. Tear-gassing and
pepper-spraying babies, children, pregnant women, and the elderly.
Shooting two innocent people dead in the street, with more injured.

What ICE did in Minnesota lays bare the sheer cruelty, violence,
authoritarianism, and incompetence of Trump’s administration.

But now, it’s our time. Our time to raise our voices high, even when the
President is speaking. Our time to fight back and defend basic American
values of freedom and justice. Our time to defeat the MAGA far-right so we
can pursue a truly progressive agenda that leaves no Americans behind.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20260226-movement.GDMDGj&refcode=em20260226-1972&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1005&akid=1972%2E342411%2EJcgRF3 ]Peter — I
need you with me if we’re going to win. Please, chip in whatever you can
afford today to the Squad Victory Fund, and supercharge our movement to
defeat Trump and his MAGA army so we can restore sanity and progress to
these United States. I am sick and tired of the lies, the violence, and
the corruption. Let’s fight back and WIN.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20260226-movement.GDMDGj&refcode=em20260226-1972&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1024&akid=1972%2E342411%2EJcgRF3 ]Contribute ››

In solidarity,

Ilhan Omar

body:
This is not just about the threats we face, but the power we have as citizens.
---

Peter, we need to be honest with ourselves in this moment.
It's important to understand the full implications of what this administration is trying to do and the threat it poses to the basic freedoms of every American. We're witnessing a deliberate attempt to erode values and norms that have made our country free and prosperous.
**But it’s not enough to simply recognize the threats we face. We also have to be clear about the power we have in a moment like this. **
The most important title in America isn’t president or senator or governor — it’s citizen. In this country, we the people have the power to determine the path forward.
Right now, some politicians have it twisted. They think they have the right to pick who their voters are so they can unfairly lock in their power in the next election.
They’re wrong. And it’s up to us to fight back against these attacks on our democracy.
**Peter, that’s why we need you in this fight.** We can't just wring our hands. We can't let cynicism get the best of us. It's our job, as Americans, to go out and do something about it. To speak out. To vote. To organize our neighbors and to understand that our best hope of solving this problem is by working together.
You know that I’ve always believed in that creed written in our founding documents and carried forward through generations: "Yes we can." And in a year like this, it takes on an even greater meaning.
When Attorney General Holder and I started Redistricting Action, we did so because we knew there would come a time when our democracy needed a grassroots movement to fight for it. [**This is that moment. And we need you with us. So if you can, make a donation to support Redistricting Action in the critical months ahead.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126201900/604217507/415011528?refcode=don_aotl_tier1_email_ObamaFeb_email_20260226-AOTL-Tier1-ObamaFeb_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260226-AOTL-Tier1-ObamaFeb_&utm_campaign=ObamaFeb&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjhhMzY4YWY3LTNjMTMtZjExMS1hNjlhLTAwMGQzYTU3NTkzZiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=4Rh9j3EDmUoxJG2v_5dYuETFtKf6f0GBam0zhOlJc9k=)

It wasn't easy telling the world I grew up dirt poor, I was raised by my Mamaw while my mother struggled with addiction.
It wasn't exactly the prep school/trust fund/summer-in-the-Hamptons upbringing that is commonplace in DC.
But I felt God called me to tell my story. Warts and all. I felt led to speak out because I believe millions of Americans share stories like mine. Stories of jobs being outsourced to China, addiction ravaging communities and killing our neighbors, and heeding the call of duty after the Towers fell on 9/11.
As your Vice President, I now stand in the breach for the left-behind, forgotten men and women who built this country, but were abandoned by the political class in DC.
I'll do everything in my power to make sure that never happens again. I'll fight every day for good folks like you.
I promise to always stand between you and the Democrat Machine that aims to obliterate everything that makes our country great.

_Defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, threatens $200m contract cut over 'woke AI.'_ **Background:** In July of 2025, the [Pentagon awarded 4 contracts of $200m each to AI companies](https://link.karlforcongress.us/69a08994/ " A BIG Step Towards AI in Warfare") OpenAI (the maker of ChatGPT), Google (Gemini), xAI (Grok), and Anthropic (Claude). The goal was to integrate AI in the operations of the US military, including its use on the battlefield. **What's happening:** The Pentagon, under Pete Hegseth, wants to use AI for [mass surveillance of US citizens and autonomous killing](https://link.karlforcongress.us/69a08a0c/ "Hegseth threatens to blacklist Anthropic over 'woke AI' concerns") with no human oversight. They want the AI companies to remove safeguards that would prevent this. **The threat:** Anthropic, an AI company that advertises itself as safety-focused, has refused to remove their safeguards. Their CEO was threatened with retaliation by Hegseth if they did not comply. Anthropic's contract would be terminated and they would be labeled a national security threat. Some sources have also reported that Hegseth intends to continue using Anthropic's AI model, even without the company's consent. Using the [Defense Production Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_Production_Act_of_1950 "Defense Production Act of 1950"), Hegseth would compel Anthropic to allow the military to use their tools "if they want to or not." **The latest:** Anthropic has been given a deadline of Friday to comply with Pete Hegseth's request or face consequences. Let's not gloss over the fact that Anthropic is the only company that is reported to have refused the request. This suggests that OpenAI, Google, and xAI have all complied and will allow their AI to perform mass surveillance and autonomously execute humans. The stakes have never been higher for having a technically competent Congress. When the Pentagon start using AI to monitor and kill, our representatives cannot stand on the sidelines. **I'm running for Congress to ensure we regulate AI** and provide oversight of the executive branch as it utilizes it in misguided and dangerous ways.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

#
Here’s where things stand in Texas with 5 days to go, Peter:
Yesterday, three new polls came out. Two showed James up, one showed him down. And turnout is at record highs all across the state.
The bottom line is this is anybody’s race to win, but we’re staying laser focused on the only poll that matters — when the votes are counted on Election Day.
**[Today is the deadline to wire money for our final ad buys, so if you can afford it, we are humbly asking you to make a contribution to take back Texas and send James Talarico to the U.S. Senate.](https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q1.AKJ3HX&refcode=em260226-1-ak&t=1&akid=475%2E1347274%2EvGUOli)**
Here’s the thing about the polls. We know there are still undecided voters. They are still considering who to vote for or whether or not they’ll even vote.
These are the people we need to reach because, in a Texas primary, it’s not just about winning the most votes. We need to get above 50% of votes in order to avoid a run-off election.
This is critical for Democrats. Everybody knows that the Republicans’ messy primary is headed to a runoff. If Democrats get a nearly 3-month head start on the general election, it’s a huge advantage. That could easily be what makes the difference in flipping this seat in November.
So we are putting every resource available into these final days. We still have huge opportunities to expand our reach across the state on television and streaming platform ads to persuade and mobilize the voters who will decide this race.
**[Please make a contribution right now to help us win big on Tuesday and put us in a position to win this seat in November. **After** Trump instituted his reckless tariff tax hikes...

**After** his administration tried to force $187 million in counterterrorism cuts on New York...

Dear Fellow American,

Chicago Public Schools desperately needs qualified teachers. But school officials are choosing to discriminate against Christian student teachers rather than fill those vacancies.

The students at Moody Bible Institute are experiencing this discrimination firsthand.

Moody's students are barred from participating in Chicago Public School's student-teaching program. Not because they lack qualifications. Not because they lack passion for serving students. But because Moody exclusively hires staff who affirm and live out its biblical beliefs.

**In other words, Chicago Public Schools is punishing Moody students for attending a college that practices its faith.**

This is an attack on religious freedom--one of the foundational freedoms that has shaped our nation since its inception. Religious schools like Moody Bible Institute have the constitutional right to exclusively hire employees who share their faith and uphold their religious mission. Without this right, religious institutions would lose their very identity and purpose.

Moody's mission is clear: proclaim the gospel and equip people to be biblically grounded, practically trained, and to engage the world through gospel-centered living. For that mission to be credible, its faculty and staff must be unified in both belief and practice.

But when Moody requested a simple religious exemption acknowledging its constitutionally protected rights, the district refused.

**Instead, officials doubled down --effectively telling Moody students that their faith disqualifies them from serving Chicago's public school children.**

Alliance Defending Freedom is representing Moody Bible Institute in a federal lawsuit to challenge this discriminatory exclusion.

**Will you sign our Statement of Support for Moody Bible Institute and stand with them in this critical moment?
**
This isn't an isolated situation. We are watching this pattern repeat nationwide.

In Washington State, **Yakima Union Gospel Mission** serves thousands of homeless individuals every day--offering food, shelter, and the hope of Christ to locals who desperately need it. Yet the state is threatening the Mission because it only hires those who share its Christian beliefs. Now the Mission is in court seeking to protect its right to hire those who share and live out its faith.

Similarly, in Oregon, Youth 71Five Ministries is asking an appeals court to protect its right to receive public benefits without having to give up its right to employ those who share its faith. Youth 71Five Ministries serves at-risk youth, empowering them with the hope of the Gospel. It depends on a staff that shares its biblical beliefs. But officials stripped the ministry of its public funding for only hiring like-minded individuals who ensure that mission goes forward, violating its constitutional freedoms.

When ministries like Moody, Yakima Union Gospel Mission, and Youth 71Five Ministries stand up in court, they are not only protecting their own freedom. They are defending religious freedom and free expression for every American--Christian or not.

**But these battles come with real emotional and personal costs.** Leaders and staff can face hostility, intense public scrutiny, and even open threats. Stand alongside thousands of believers who are praying for Moody during these stressful times.

clean_body: Chicago Public Schools desperately needs qualified teachers. ' | Please see a special message from our sponsor. If you would like to unsubscribe, visit this | | | Dear Fellow American, Chicago Public Schools desperately needs qualified teachers. But school officials are choosing to discriminate against Christian student teachers rather than fill those vacancies. The students at Moody Bible Institute are experiencing this discrimination firsthand. Moody's students are barred from participating in Chicago Public School's student-teaching program. Not because they lack qualifications. Not because they lack passion for serving students. But because Moody exclusively hires staff who affirm and live out its biblical beliefs. In other words, Chicago Public Schools is punishing Moody students for attending a college that practices its faith. This is an attack on religious freedom--one of the foundational freedoms that has shaped our nation since its inception. Religious schools like Moody Bible Institute have the constitutional right to exclusively hire employees who share their faith and uphold their religious mission. Without this right, religious institutions would lose their very identity and purpose. Moody's mission is clear: proclaim the gospel and equip people to be biblically grounded, practically trained, and to engage the world through gospel-centered living. For that mission to be credible, its faculty and staff must be unified in both belief and practice. But when Moody requested a simple religious exemption acknowledging its constitutionally protected rights, the district refused. Instead, officials doubled down --effectively telling Moody students that their faith disqualifies them from serving Chicago's public school children. Alliance Defending Freedom is representing Moody Bible Institute in a federal lawsuit to challenge this discriminatory exclusion. Will you sign our Statement of Support for Moody Bible Institute and stand with them in this critical moment? This isn't an isolated situation. We are watching this pattern repeat nationwide. In Washington State, Yakima Union Gospel Mission serves thousands of homeless individuals every day--offering food, shelter, and the hope of Christ to locals who desperately need it. Yet the state is threatening the Mission because it only hires those who share its Christian beliefs. Now the Mission is in court seeking to protect its right to hire those who share and live out its faith. Similarly, in Oregon, Youth 71Five Ministries is asking an appeals court to protect its right to receive public benefits without having to give up its right to employ those who share its faith. Youth 71Five Ministries serves at-risk youth, empowering them with the hope of the Gospel. It depends on a staff that shares its biblical beliefs. But officials stripped the ministry of its public funding for only hiring like-minded individuals who ensure that mission goes forward, violating its constitutional freedoms. When ministries like Moody, Yakima Union Gospel Mission, and Youth 71Five Ministries stand up in court, they are not only protecting their own freedom. They are defending religious freedom and free expression for every American--Christian or not. But these battles come with real emotional and personal costs. Leaders and staff can face hostility, intense public scrutiny, and even open threats. Stand alongside thousands of believers who are praying for Moody during these stressful times. That's why your voice matters so deeply right now. Please take a moment to sign the Statement of Support today. Thank you for standing with those who are standing for truth. For freedom, Jeremiah Galus Senior Counsel Alliance Defending Freedom Alliance Defending Freedom 15100 N. 90th Street, Scottsdale, Arizona 85260

# [WEF CEO quits over Epstein dinner bombshell](https://substack.com/redirect/9b1a461f-51d6-4095-8010-cb5b89af266c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Børge Brende, president and CEO of the World Economic Forum since 2017, resigned Thursday after U.S. Justice Department disclosures revealed **[three business dinners and email/text exchanges with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein,](https://substack.com/redirect/9b1a461f-51d6-4095-8010-cb5b89af266c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** prompting an independent WEF investigation that found no further concerns but led Brende to step down to avoid distractions for the organization.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9b1a461f-51d6-4095-8010-cb5b89af266c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Epstein ties exposed:** U.S. Justice Department files detailed Brende's three business dinners with Epstein in 2018-2019 plus communications via email and text messages.
* **WEF launches probe:** The organization initiated an independent review by outside counsel weeks ago after the disclosures surfaced, concluding with no additional issues beyond known contacts.
* **Interim leadership named:** Alois Zwinggi, a WEF managing board member, was appointed interim president and CEO while the Board of Trustees seeks a permanent successor.
* **Brende 's farewell statement:** The former Norwegian foreign minister cited 81⁄2 rewarding years and stepped down "after careful consideration" without mentioning Epstein, emphasizing focus on the Forum's ongoing work.

# [Amazon Web Services crashed because AI deleted the code on its own](https://substack.com/redirect/1c6b8892-a202-41e9-a81f-353370a93018?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Amazon's internal AI coding agent autonomously deleted and recreated a live production environment in December, **[triggering a 13-hour outage on AWS services](https://substack.com/redirect/1c6b8892-a202-41e9-a81f-353370a93018?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and exposing risks of unchecked agentic AI in critical cloud infrastructure.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1c6b8892-a202-41e9-a81f-353370a93018?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Agentic Tool Autonomy Exposed:** Amazon's Kiro AI, designed for independent actions, evaluated a production issue and opted to wipe and rebuild the entire environment without human oversight.
* **Outage Scope Limited:** The December incident disrupted AWS Cost Explorer in mainland China regions for 13 hours, sparing broader compute, storage, and database services from impact.
* **Amazon Blames Configuration:** Company insists the disruption stemmed from user misconfigured access controls, not AI failure, calling it coincidental that AI tools were involved in multiple recent outages.
* **Broader AI Adoption Risks:** As Amazon pushes for 80% developer use of AI coding tools, the foreseeable yet preventable incidents highlight governance gaps in granting autonomous systems operator-level permissions in production.

# [Chinese robot vacuum army exposed thousands of homes LIVE](https://substack.com/redirect/6e2eedfc-17d5-49af-86e0-d5eb612ebf72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A security flaw in DJI's Chinese-made Romo robot vacuum briefly granted one researcher **[unauthorized access to live camera feeds, microphones, and floor plans](https://substack.com/redirect/6e2eedfc-17d5-49af-86e0-d5eb612ebf72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** from nearly 7,000 devices in homes across 24 countries, including the US.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6e2eedfc-17d5-49af-86e0-d5eb612ebf72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **MQTT Broker Flaw Exposed:** A permission validation error in DJI's cloud MQTT system allowed wildcard subscriptions, enabling a single credential to access all device data in plaintext despite TLS encryption.
* **Researcher Demo Revealed Scale:** Security tinkerer Azdoufal, experimenting with custom controls, unintentionally viewed real-time feeds from thousands of vacuums worldwide within minutes during a live test.
* **DJI Issued Swift Patches:** The company detected the issue internally in late January, deploying automatic fixes on February 8 and 10, 2026, requiring no user intervention to secure affected devices.
* **Privacy Risks Highlighted:** Incident underscores dangers of foreign-controlled cloud infrastructure mapping intimate home layouts, fueling US concerns over Chinese tech sovereignty and data security in consumer devices.

# [Lamborghini ditches its first EV before launch, calls it an expensive hobby](https://substack.com/redirect/a77105c8-5df6-4bbc-bb23-c9da42c65d03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Lamborghini has **[scrapped plans to launch its first all-electric vehicle,](https://substack.com/redirect/a77105c8-5df6-4bbc-bb23-c9da42c65d03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the Lanzador, originally slated for 2028, after CEO Stephan Winkelmann cited "close to zero" demand among luxury buyers who crave the emotional roar of combustion engines. The Italian supercar maker will pivot to a plug-in hybrid instead.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a77105c8-5df6-4bbc-bb23-c9da42c65d03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **EV Demand Collapses:** Acceptance for full EVs among Lamborghini's clientele is near zero and flattening, prompting the cancellation of the Lanzador project after internal analysis.
* **Emotional Connection Key:** Current EVs fail to deliver the thrilling "emotional experience" that customers demand from supercars, unlike traditional engines.
* **Hybrid Pivot Planned:** The scrapped Lanzador will be replaced by a plug-in hybrid electric vehicle as Lamborghini targets PHEVs for its lineup through 2030.
* **Combustion Commitment Stays:** The company vows to produce internal combustion engine vehicles for as long as possible while keeping future EV options open only "when the time is right."

# [Nvidia unveils Vera Rubin AI beast crushes Blackwell efficiency](https://substack.com/redirect/1ac3070c-82cc-446a-86b7-ce0e741f2a26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nvidia gave CNBC an exclusive first look at Vera Rubin, **[its next-generation rack-scale AI system set to ship in the second half of 2026.](https://substack.com/redirect/1ac3070c-82cc-446a-86b7-ce0e741f2a26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** The platform delivers 10 times more performance per watt than predecessor Grace Blackwell--despite roughly double the power draw--through full liquid cooling and modular design, addressing surging AI energy demands amid fierce competition.-
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1ac3070c-82cc-446a-86b7-ce0e741f2a26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Massive modular build** : Vera Rubin rack integrates 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs with 1.3 million components from over 80 global suppliers, enabling easy slide-out repairs unlike soldered Blackwell parts.
* **Breakthrough efficiency leap** : Achieves 10x better performance per watt via 100% liquid cooling that slashes data center water use, even as total power consumption doubles compared to Grace Blackwell.
* **Production and rollout timeline** : Already in full production after January 2026 announcement, with shipments starting second half of 2026 and major adopters like Meta targeting 2027 data center deployments.
* **Competitive supply chain edge** : NVIDIA coordinates detailed forecasts across 20+ countries to combat memory shortages, while facing rivals like AMD's Helios and custom chips from hyperscalers such as Google and Amazon.

clean_body: | Friend, Most of us don’t need a long list of rules to live by. For me, it really comes down to two things: 1) Act like a grown-up and 2) Don’t be a jerk. (Pretty basic, right?) 😉 And yet, if you’ve turned on the news lately, you know these basics are in short supply... Too often, the focus is on scoring points instead of solving problems. Meanwhile, families in mid-Michigan are worried about their grocery bills, their health care costs, and protecting the Social Security and Medicare benefits they’ve earned. That’s the work I’m focused on every day – lowering costs, standing up for seniors, and making sure working families in MI-08 can get ahead. And when there’s an opportunity to work across the aisle to get something done for our district, I take it. Because results matter. But the political reality is that MI-08 is one of the most competitive districts in the country. National Republicans see this seat as a top pickup opportunity, and they’re already spending big to try to flip it. clean_body: I make the political class nervous. That’s why they are coming after me. | Peter, I am going to be straight with you. Our Texas primary is less than one week from today. The establishment is pulling out all the stops to defeat me - because I have never been afraid to stand up to the Swamp in Washington. I've taken on both parties - and that hasn't made things easy. I've stood up to the swamp to ban stock trading by members of Congress - because public service should never be a get-rich scheme. I've fought to keep our elections free, fair, and secure - because confidence in our system in the foundation of our Republic. And I've worked to protect our communities and defend the rule of law and American values here at home. This kind of leadership makes the political class nervous. The lobbyists. Career Politicians. But I don't answer to them, Peter. I answer to YOU and the American patriots across the country who deserve better from Washington. With less than 7 days before our Primary, I need every conservative who believes in limited government, secure elections, and real accountability to step up. I need you by my side. Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Axios: Dominion Voting sold to company run by ex-GOP election official [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA007/1/89215/images/Axios_DominionVotingSale.png]
Axios recently broke news that Dominion Voting Systems — makers of voting machines used in 27 states for elections across the country — has been sold to a Missouri-based company run by a former Republican election official.
Scott Leiendecker is the owner of KNOWiNK, which is changing its corporate name to "Liberty Vote", and has previously been appointed by Missouri officials to investigate the 2000 election and be " St. Louis' Republican election director ."
Leiendecker told Axios in a statement that his company is " committed to delivering election technology that prioritizes paper-based transparency, security and simplicity so that voters can be assured that every ballot is filled-in accurately and fairly counted ."
We want to hear from supporters in your area about this tactic. Will you take our one-click poll right away?

clean_body: Voter Action Project [] Axios: Dominion Voting sold to company run by ex-GOP election official [] Axios recently broke news that Dominion Voting Systems — makers of voting machines used in 27 states for elections across the country — has been sold to a Missouri-based company run by a former Republican election official. Scott Leiendecker is the owner of KNOWiNK, which is changing its corporate name to "Liberty Vote", and has previously been appointed by Missouri officials to investigate the 2000 election and be " St. Louis' Republican election director ." Leiendecker told Axios in a statement that his company is " committed to delivering election technology that prioritizes paper-based transparency, security and simplicity so that voters can be assured that every ballot is filled-in accurately and fairly counted ." We want to hear from supporters in your area about this tactic. Will you take our one-click poll right away? Team: Are you worried about partisan ownership of voting machine companies? **Former Congressman and Lt. Col. Allen West, one of America’s most respected conservative warriors, has personally endorsed my campaign for Congress!**

✅**Fully fund and modernize our military** so our troops never go into battle under-equipped.
✅**Expand VA healthcare** , mental health support, and real job opportunities for veterans—no one who served should ever be forgotten.
✅**Cut wasteful spending and balance the budget** so we can afford the strong defense our nation needs.

The U.S. Citizenship Act of 2021 ([H.R. 1177/S. 348](https://substack.com/redirect/94b0daaf-0815-4124-82c0-061cb79f001d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)), introduced by [Rep. Linda Sanchez](https://substack.com/redirect/36f25a88-c6ad-41a7-b3b3-0b72f13141b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the House and former [Senator Bob Menendez](https://substack.com/redirect/cc173053-5fde-4882-9077-ef03ca3ecee0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), on President Biden's first day in office, represented one of the most ambitious attempts at [comprehensive immigration reform](https://substack.com/redirect/145312d4-c70d-4f33-b7e2-61c6ecf7c463?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in decades. Unveiled on January 20, 2021, via a [White House fact sheet](https://substack.com/redirect/6ddc6886-0d6a-4c91-a835-672b13c181ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the bill promised to "modernize our immigration system" by offering an earned pathway to citizenship for an estimated 11 million undocumented immigrants, bolstering border security through technology, and overhauling family- and employment-based visas.

Proponents hailed it as a humane response to decades of legislative inaction, addressing border czarina Vice President Harris' [root causes](https://substack.com/redirect/d22d2566-7383-4b53-b2e1-6f77126b99cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of migration while integrating long-term residents into American society. Yet, the bill stalled in Congress, failing to advance beyond initial committee referrals due to deep partisan divides--a pattern echoing failed reforms like the [2006](https://substack.com/redirect/45dc7558-a628-4ce0-a43f-6e141c8c3da2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [2013](https://substack.com/redirect/5c220350-d265-4e00-970a-d0a8e014c21c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) efforts.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.9Zf7lY4UIN1aI44TSTrQ5NA6YUK6HAS2D1rHW_hSAQc?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=189287208)
Republicans decried it as "amnesty" that would incentivize further illegal entries, while Democrats lamented the lack of bipartisan buy-in.

This assessment argues that the bill's failure, far from a tragedy, averted a potential deluge of unauthorized migration that could have overwhelmed U.S. borders and strained resources. Instead, the Biden administration's subsequent "[Blueprint for a Fair, Orderly, and Humane Immigration System](https://substack.com/redirect/81688f6b-aef2-4344-a389-fdcf53b2636f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," outlined in a July 27, 2021, fact sheet, forced a more restrained executive-led framework.

By prioritizing enforcement, regional deterrence, and targeted legal pathways without blanket amnesty, the blueprint--bolstered by over 600 immigration-related executive actions--stabilized the system and "saved" America from the flood of illegals that critics warned the Citizenship Act would unleash.

This pragmatic pivot, though imperfect, underscores how legislative overreach can backfire, while calibrated executive measures can restore order amid political gridlock.

To understand the stakes, consider the Citizenship Act's core provisions, as detailed in the January 2021 fact sheet. At its heart was a multi-tiered pathway to citizenship for undocumented individuals present in the U.S. before January 1, 2021. Eligible applicants--subject to criminal and security checks, tax compliance, and physical presence requirements--could secure temporary protected status, transition to green cards after five years, and apply for naturalization after three more, including English and civics tests.

Special expedited tracks applied to Dreamers (DACA recipients), TPS holders, and farmworkers, allowing immediate green card applications. The bill explicitly changed "alien" to "noncitizen" in statutes, signaling a philosophical shift toward viewing immigrants as integral to America's identity as a "nation of immigrants.

"Beyond legalization, the Act targeted systemic bottlenecks. It aimed to clear employment-based visa backlogs by recapturing unused visas, eliminating per-country caps, and exempting STEM graduates from U.S. universities. Dependents of H-1B holders would gain work authorization to prevent "aging out," while a new commission would refine employment verification to curb exploitation. Family-based reforms similarly recaptured visas, raised per-country limits, and scrapped the "3- and 10-year bars" that separated sponsors from relatives abroad. Protections extended to LGBTQ+ partnerships, orphans, and Filipino WWII veterans, with parole programs for Central American reunifications.

Border security and enforcement were not ignored; the bill allocated funds for high-tech scanning at ports of entry to detect drugs and contraband, flexible surveillance along the southern border, and infrastructure to process asylum seekers.

It cracked down on smuggling via enhanced prosecutions and sanctions, funded rescue beacons to curb migrant deaths, and established oversight for agent misconduct. Root causes received $4 billion over four years for Central America, conditioned on anti-corruption efforts, alongside Designated Processing Centers for refugee screenings. Other reforms expanded U visas for crime victims to 30,000 annually, hiked diversity visa caps to 80,000, and funded integration programs like English classes.

On paper, this was a sweeping vision: humane integration meets fortified enforcement. But the bill's fate was sealed by February 2021, when Senate Republicans blocked debate, citing insufficient border measures and fears of rewarding lawbreaking.

Historical precedents loomed large; comprehensive bills had crumbled under similar weight, from the [1986 Immigration Reform and Control Act's](https://substack.com/redirect/193971ec-6b42-43ce-872e-6bf9d96b0334?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) unfulfilled enforcement promises to the 2013 Senate bill's House demise.

The 117th Congress, narrowly Democratic-controlled, prioritized COVID relief and infrastructure, sidelining immigration amid rising partisan rancor.
Polling showed broad public support for Dreamer protections but sharp divides on broader amnesty, with Republicans overwhelmingly opposing pathways for undocumented adults.

Conservative critiques amplified these fissures, framing the Act not as reform but as a magnet for chaos. The Heritage Foundation's February 2021 analysis lambasted it for "erasing the distinction between legal and illegal immigration," granting amnesty to millions--including those with criminal records--without robust security triggers.
Critics argued the bill's tech-focused border investments paled against physical barriers, while visa expansions would flood labor markets, undercutting wages for low-skilled Americans. "It would increase both illegal and legal immigration," Heritage warned, predicting a surge in chain migration as newly legalized immigrants sponsor relatives.

Echoing broader debates, outlets like Britannica highlighted how such policies "reward" lawbreakers, eroding deterrence and straining public services.

Pew Research captured the zeitgeist: by May 2021, 68% of Americans criticized federal border handling, with Republicans viewing amnesty as an open invitation.
These concerns were not abstract. Post-inauguration border encounters spiked from 75,000 in January 2021 to over 173,000 by March, coinciding with the bill's introduction and perceptions of lax enforcement.

Had the Act passed, conservatives posited, its amnesty promise--publicized globally--would have amplified "pull factors," drawing record caravans from Central America and beyond. Historical analogs, like the 1986 amnesty's aftermath of renewed surges, fueled this narrative.

Even bipartisan analyses, such as from the Bipartisan Policy Center, noted the bill's high-skilled focus overlooked vulnerabilities to mass low-skilled inflows.
Enter the Biden administration's July 2021 blueprint, a fact sheet that recalibrated ambitions into executable reality.

Absent congressional action, it pivoted to executive levers: "redirect[ing] resources from border wall construction to... smarter security measures" like port modernization and anti-smuggling ops via Operation Sentinel.

Enforcement emphasized "fair" application, deploying 19,500 Border Patrol agents while rescinding Trump-era asylum curbs, yet streamlining expedited removals for ineligible claimants. Border management targeted "unique encounters" below 2019 levels through regional training and infrastructure aid, deterring irregular flows via public messaging campaigns.

Legal pathways expanded selectively: restarting the Central American Minors program, boosting H-2A/B visas for seasonal workers, and cutting Northern Triangle backlogs, all without the Act's mass citizenship track.

Protections focused on vulnerability--$255 million in Central American aid for food insecurity and violence prevention, plus pro bono legal aid to slash court backlogs. [Root causes loomed large](https://substack.com/redirect/fefa11e0-40cd-4170-9e2d-4f80c1ee488d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): $861 million for economic growth, governance, and anti-corruption in El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras, paired with Migration Resource Centers for lawful referrals.

This blueprint, operationalized through executive orders like the February 2021 directive on regional frameworks, addressed migration's "causes" via diplomacy and deterrence, not domestic legalization.

Early actions included revoking Trump travel bans and prioritizing enforcement on threats, not families.

By mid-2021, these yielded mixed but stabilizing results. Encounters peaked at 2.4 million in FY 2023 amid global disruptions, but the blueprint's emphasis on removals--over 1.5 million in FY 2022--curbed net inflows.

Critics, including Senate hearings, blamed initial "pull factors" like paused deportations for the surge, yet later restrictions--like the June 2024 executive order capping asylum at 2,500 daily crossings--slashed encounters 94% from February 2024 peaks by early 2025.

Data substantiates the blueprint's salvific role. Under Trump, FY 2020 encounters hit 400,000; Biden's first year saw 1.7 million, correlating with policy signals.
But by FY 2024, post-blueprint tweaks like 20 miles of new barriers and hemispheric pacts, daily averages dropped below 2,000--below pre-Biden norms.
The Migration Policy Institute notes a shift: unauthorized port encounters rose from 4% in FY 2021 to higher legal processing, reducing chaotic between-port rushes.
Fentanyl seizures hit records, undercutting smuggling networks the blueprint targeted.

Without the Act's amnesty beacon, these measures--$4 billion in root-cause aid realized via executive channels--dampened caravans, sparing cities like New York and Chicago the 2023 shelter crises from unchecked releases.

Critics might counter that the blueprint was reactive, not preventive, with surges exposing enforcement gaps. Yet, compared to the Act's hypothetical: amnesty for 11 million could have spiked applications by 20-30%, per Heritage models, overwhelming USCIS and incentivizing "catch-and-release" gaming.

The blueprint's narrower scope--expanding targeted visas while expelling 3 million+--maintained deterrence, fostering a 2025 environment where encounters plummeted 71% month-over-month.

Gallup polls reflect abatement in immigration concerns by mid-2025, reversing 2021 spikes.

In retrospect, the Citizenship Act's failure was [fortuitous](https://substack.com/redirect/865dde85-286b-45b4-9d0d-87a6e973fb65?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with October 2025 closing out **the fiscal year with the lowest U.S. Border Patrol apprehensions since 1970**.

Its grand bargain--amnesty for enforcement--crumbled under scrutiny, revealing how legislative utopias can court disaster in a polarized era. The blueprint, by contrast, embodied executive realism: humane yet firm, collaborative yet controlled. It invested in prevention abroad, streamlined removals at home, and expanded legal vents without flooding the system. Over 605 actions later, Biden's tenure ended with a border more secure than inherited, averting the "invasion" conservatives feared.
This saga teaches that true reform lies in balance, not boldness alone. America dodged a deluge, thanks to the blueprint's steady hand--proving that sometimes, failure is the ultimate safeguard.

Nothing says "border control" like offering 11 million people a fast pass to citizenship. | | | Feb 26 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- The U.S. Citizenship Act of 2021 (), introduced by in the House and former , on President Biden's first day in office, represented one of the most ambitious attempts at in decades. Unveiled on January 20, 2021, via a , the bill promised to "modernize our immigration system" by offering an earned pathway to citizenship for an estimated 11 million undocumented immigrants, bolstering border security through technology, and overhauling family- and employment-based visas. Proponents hailed it as a humane response to decades of legislative inaction, addressing border czarina Vice President Harris' of migration while integrating long-term residents into American society. Yet, the bill stalled in Congress, failing to advance beyond initial committee referrals due to deep partisan divides--a pattern echoing failed reforms like the and efforts. Republicans decried it as "amnesty" that would incentivize further illegal entries, while Democrats lamented the lack of bipartisan buy-in. This assessment argues that the bill's failure, far from a tragedy, averted a potential deluge of unauthorized migration that could have overwhelmed U.S. borders and strained resources. Instead, the Biden administration's subsequent "," outlined in a July 27, 2021, fact sheet, forced a more restrained executive-led framework. By prioritizing enforcement, regional deterrence, and targeted legal pathways without blanket amnesty, the blueprint--bolstered by over 600 immigration-related executive actions--stabilized the system and "saved" America from the flood of illegals that critics warned the Citizenship Act would unleash. This pragmatic pivot, though imperfect, underscores how legislative overreach can backfire, while calibrated executive measures can restore order amid political gridlock. To understand the stakes, consider the Citizenship Act's core provisions, as detailed in the January 2021 fact sheet. At its heart was a multi-tiered pathway to citizenship for undocumented individuals present in the U.S. before January 1, 2021. Eligible applicants--subject to criminal and security checks, tax compliance, and physical presence requirements--could secure temporary protected status, transition to green cards after five years, and apply for naturalization after three more, including English and civics tests. Special expedited tracks applied to Dreamers (DACA recipients), TPS holders, and farmworkers, allowing immediate green card applications. The bill explicitly changed "alien" to "noncitizen" in statutes, signaling a philosophical shift toward viewing immigrants as integral to America's identity as a "nation of immigrants. "Beyond legalization, the Act targeted systemic bottlenecks. It aimed to clear employment-based visa backlogs by recapturing unused visas, eliminating per-country caps, and exempting STEM graduates from U.S. universities. Dependents of H-1B holders would gain work authorization to prevent "aging out," while a new commission would refine employment verification to curb exploitation. Family-based reforms similarly recaptured visas, raised per-country limits, and scrapped the "3- and 10-year bars" that separated sponsors from relatives abroad. Protections extended to LGBTQ+ partnerships, orphans, and Filipino WWII veterans, with parole programs for Central American reunifications. Border security and enforcement were not ignored; the bill allocated funds for high-tech scanning at ports of entry to detect drugs and contraband, flexible surveillance along the southern border, and infrastructure to process asylum seekers. It cracked down on smuggling via enhanced prosecutions and sanctions, funded rescue beacons to curb migrant deaths, and established oversight for agent misconduct. Root causes received $4 billion over four years for Central America, conditioned on anti-corruption efforts, alongside Designated Processing Centers for refugee screenings. Other reforms expanded U visas for crime victims to 30,000 annually, hiked diversity visa caps to 80,000, and funded integration programs like English classes. On paper, this was a sweeping vision: humane integration meets fortified enforcement. But the bill's fate was sealed by February 2021, when Senate Republicans blocked debate, citing insufficient border measures and fears of rewarding lawbreaking. Historical precedents loomed large; comprehensive bills had crumbled under similar weight, from the unfulfilled enforcement promises to the 2013 Senate bill's House demise. The 117th Congress, narrowly Democratic-controlled, prioritized COVID relief and infrastructure, sidelining immigration amid rising partisan rancor. Polling showed broad public support for Dreamer protections but sharp divides on broader amnesty, with Republicans overwhelmingly opposing pathways for undocumented adults. Conservative critiques amplified these fissures, framing the Act not as reform but as a magnet for chaos. The Heritage Foundation's February 2021 analysis lambasted it for "erasing the distinction between legal and illegal immigration," granting amnesty to millions--including those with criminal records--without robust security triggers. Critics argued the bill's tech-focused border investments paled against physical barriers, while visa expansions would flood labor markets, undercutting wages for low-skilled Americans. "It would increase both illegal and legal immigration," Heritage warned, predicting a surge in chain migration as newly legalized immigrants sponsor relatives. Echoing broader debates, outlets like Britannica highlighted how such policies "reward" lawbreakers, eroding deterrence and straining public services. Pew Research captured the zeitgeist: by May 2021, 68% of Americans criticized federal border handling, with Republicans viewing amnesty as an open invitation. These concerns were not abstract. Post-inauguration border encounters spiked from 75,000 in January 2021 to over 173,000 by March, coinciding with the bill's introduction and perceptions of lax enforcement. Had the Act passed, conservatives posited, its amnesty promise--publicized globally--would have amplified "pull factors," drawing record caravans from Central America and beyond. Historical analogs, like the 1986 amnesty's aftermath of renewed surges, fueled this narrative. Even bipartisan analyses, such as from the Bipartisan Policy Center, noted the bill's high-skilled focus overlooked vulnerabilities to mass low-skilled inflows. Enter the Biden administration's July 2021 blueprint, a fact sheet that recalibrated ambitions into executable reality. Absent congressional action, it pivoted to executive levers: "redirect[ing] resources from border wall construction to... smarter security measures" like port modernization and anti-smuggling ops via Operation Sentinel. Enforcement emphasized "fair" application, deploying 19,500 Border Patrol agents while rescinding Trump-era asylum curbs, yet streamlining expedited removals for ineligible claimants. Border management targeted "unique encounters" below 2019 levels through regional training and infrastructure aid, deterring irregular flows via public messaging campaigns. Legal pathways expanded selectively: restarting the Central American Minors program, boosting H-2A/B visas for seasonal workers, and cutting Northern Triangle backlogs, all without the Act's mass citizenship track. Protections focused on vulnerability--$255 million in Central American aid for food insecurity and violence prevention, plus pro bono legal aid to slash court backlogs. : $861 million for economic growth, governance, and anti-corruption in El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras, paired with Migration Resource Centers for lawful referrals. This blueprint, operationalized through executive orders like the February 2021 directive on regional frameworks, addressed migration's "causes" via diplomacy and deterrence, not domestic legalization. Early actions included revoking Trump travel bans and prioritizing enforcement on threats, not families. By mid-2021, these yielded mixed but stabilizing results. Encounters peaked at 2.4 million in FY 2023 amid global disruptions, but the blueprint's emphasis on removals--over 1.5 million in FY 2022--curbed net inflows. Critics, including Senate hearings, blamed initial "pull factors" like paused deportations for the surge, yet later restrictions--like the June 2024 executive order capping asylum at 2,500 daily crossings--slashed encounters 94% from February 2024 peaks by early 2025. Data substantiates the blueprint's salvific role. Under Trump, FY 2020 encounters hit 400,000; Biden's first year saw 1.7 million, correlating with policy signals. But by FY 2024, post-blueprint tweaks like 20 miles of new barriers and hemispheric pacts, daily averages dropped below 2,000--below pre-Biden norms. The Migration Policy Institute notes a shift: unauthorized port encounters rose from 4% in FY 2021 to higher legal processing, reducing chaotic between-port rushes. Fentanyl seizures hit records, undercutting smuggling networks the blueprint targeted. Without the Act's amnesty beacon, these measures--$4 billion in root-cause aid realized via executive channels--dampened caravans, sparing cities like New York and Chicago the 2023 shelter crises from unchecked releases. Critics might counter that the blueprint was reactive, not preventive, with surges exposing enforcement gaps. ---
|
---
Hi friend,

I’m Sue — but you probably already know that. You also probably know that I’m on the Providence City Council because you signed up for my email updates.

But what you might not realize (yet!) is that in November, I launched my campaign for Rhode Island’s Lieutenant Governor. And that’s why I’m writing to you today to ask for this chance: **[can I earn your vote?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3865u5P-T9YITnie-ESWxWXrlDLv6wmj_pBkmXxvJgZC3Yw5g0LSNsiwmuUs8edZe-lJsj2zApT-MkajCXKAxjRmuwP9j-puSuoP959H5t1RVj0Wtj9_opxgwYuvefMGKNWijuL7qCW4vxRGhCt3ZQyDitQ57sd0UByuzGK-cTNpW6tmMNRWDdfGX6RDoVEaomdcYKIAn_tri3ahNjG4961x9UZtRwT6GZAPy77s9SFHjvLDGWBDRU86LMSTFt604Cqy27tnrGqC44HOTi-QCGvg0wW6Osj7VtGkye5VgaYSTupfjEolj2rAbEJJS3nANS4BmOwGczIPh8Z5m-tq0LK/4oh/UJqpGzRMTSi1GbWMqkvjyg/h0/h001.aOEy_AOuQ2PVfitIRm_gpzkm4Ko6H22FODFQ-d1mp8E)**

As someone who has connected with me as a council member, you’ve already seen how I show up for Rhode Island and the kind of leader I aspire to be. I also hope you’ve seen the impact of the work I’ve done to make your life — and our community! — better.

**That’s exactly why I’m running for LG.**

Honestly, friend, you are the reason. You deserve leadership that is accessible, transparent, and grounded in real work. I believe public service is a responsibility. And I have a responsibility to make our lives better.

That’s why I hope I already know the answer to this question, but I want you to answer me truthfully: **[can I earn your vote in my race to be Rhode Island’s next Lieutenant Governor?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3865u5P-T9YITnie-ESWxWXrlDLv6wmj_pBkmXxvJgZC3Yw5g0LSNsiwmuUs8edZe-lJsj2zApT-MkajCXKAxjRmuwP9j-puSuoP959H5t1RVj0Wtj9_opxgwYuvefMGKNR-WXsSHYDr4BEZkRAOk1REzjG0-aM_o1He1CsShrr36wXGcK_bPIC0Qjfl9J9T97vP92KDmFndc2i46Df-kjoGFVh_Cv2J5BL2a_ps7wv-_PN8LmYpdYRZmyLUBTtuTlPth6gyZro-lcblmeKPVltRw6v5iq4QAXZmmvm4GTs9D_mJZhnW08g98IpZ6cq1oeuxrSGISWQPODCnmubjLgO/4oh/UJqpGzRMTSi1GbWMqkvjyg/h1/h001.oZzmel0Q2ZV8v9U0CdcaqJYztDiU5MyzpW6DUn0avMs)** | | [ **I'M WITH YOU!** ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3865u5P-T9YITnie-ESWxWXrlDLv6wmj_pBkmXxvJgZC3Yw5g0LSNsiwmuUs8edZe-lJsj2zApT-MkajCXKAxjRmuwP9j-puSuoP959H5t1RVj0Wtj9_opxgwYuvefMGKNbgOOyn9c_rU8SWu1oOe1if9ecvibbHwGcDaeepDBWYDlNnSb-9LRt-S4YAmdN3Egmfeit0RqAvJzBm1GSXnub2pS1wdZPLDLusCvi2RPcGXnib_b_TBIergWqorYbZ2Y4SOpbxV-t6eGJt4oPinwlF77d5zq8PuXNAuCuz_EcEVhGZ_ql38mayLsuH6CWT3qJdgj_Ocb-3ovkC-SkhbEl/4oh/UJqpGzRMTSi1GbWMqkvjyg/h2/h001.OK5J5FdAzU-mh-a8q6S1wVKVXYEOw_vA6FfQcgxjKxM)

name: Aaron Ford
subject: I need your help, friend
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
My name is Aaron Ford, and I’m running for Governor of Nevada to fight for hardworking families.

| | |
---
Friend,
My name is Aaron Ford, and I’m running for Governor of Nevada to fight for hardworking families.**In a moment,[I’m going to ask you to split a donation between Deb Haaland's grassroots campaign and mine](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5749?refcode=jtk282-bu-nd&t=1&akid=7796%2E400544%2E-28ZGj) — but first, let me share my story with you.**
**_I grew up in a working-class family._**
The neighborhoods I come from are tough. My dad stocked produce at Safeway, and my mom worked odd jobs to help keep us afloat. Sometimes, dinner was just a stale candy bar.

I became a dad in college — then, a single dad shortly after. My son and I relied on Medicaid and food stamps, and I continued pursuing my education. I _never_ gave up.

I earned five degrees, became a public school math teacher, and got elected to the Nevada state Senate, where I was both Minority Leader and Majority Leader during my tenure. **Today, I’m humbled to serve as Nevada’s Attorney General.**
**_Gov. Lombardo has failed us._**
While I’ve worked to make life better and more affordable for every Nevadan in every neighborhood, Republican Gov. Joe Lombardo has done the exact opposite.

He has vetoed housing reform in the middle of a housing crisis, blocked a cap on prescription drug prices at a time when costs are through the roof, and rejected free school meals for our kids. **And Lombardo continues to stand by Donald Trump and his harmful MAGA agenda.**
Nevadans are fed up and ready for change.

_The Cook Political Report_ ranks this race a Toss Up and says that Lombardo is the most vulnerable Republican Governor of the midterm elections. **In fact, this race is Democrats’ best opportunity to flip a gubernatorial seat blue across the country.**
**_It’s time to move forward, and I need your help._**
I’m proof of what’s possible when government sees people not as numbers, but as neighbors. When a family gets a fair shot. When elected leaders make sure that folks who are struggling but striving — like I once was — have the tools they need to chase their dreams.

We’re not getting any of that from Joe Lombardo, which is why I’m running for Governor.

Together, I _know_ we can build a Nevada where everyone who calls our great state home can succeed. But it won’t be easy, and it’ll take serious resources.
**The GOP is going to spend millions to defeat me and protect their power. And since Lombardo recently launched his reelection campaign, MAGA special interests are gearing up to flood this race with an influx of cash to tip the scales in their direction as early as possible.**
**[The only way I’ll be able to compete and win is with your support, friend. So please, will you chip in now to Deb Haaland and me to help me flip this key gubernatorial seat blue and move Nevada forward?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5749?refcode=jtk282-bu-nd&t=2&akid=7796%2E400544%2E-28ZGj)**
| | [Contribute](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5749?refcode=jtk282-bu-nd&t=3&akid=7796%2E400544%2E-28ZGj)
---
Thank you so much. I’m incredibly grateful.

Aaron Ford

# Tonight is County Convention Night - Let’s Make Michigan Red!
---
| | I hope this email finds you and your family well. I'm truly grateful for the incredible support we're seeing across Michigan as we build toward the March endorsement convention. It's an honor to earn the trust of grassroots Republicans like you who are fighting for our shared America First values.
**Tonight is the big night** — county conventions across Michigan where we select our state delegates and alternates for the March endorsement convention.
I recorded a short personal message for all of you about **why this moment is so important**. [Please take a moment to watch it below by clicking on the image:](https://kevinformi.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=39782b0ca6b504d2faad7a196&id=edffa36f28&e=4b10910eed)
[](https://kevinformi.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=39782b0ca6b504d2faad7a196&id=9990fcfa2d&e=4b10910eed)
If you stand with me to end Dana Nessel’s extreme lawfare, restore election integrity, protect parental rights, and deliver real results for Michigan families, **I humbly ask you to stand to be elected a delegate at your local county convention tonight**.
We’ve continue to build tremendous momentum — **landslide Ottawa County endorsement (106-6)** , **Berrien County straw poll win by over 30 points** ,**Mackinac Conference commanding straw poll win** , **Wayne 12th straw poll win** , and now the powerful endorsement of **Dr. John Eastman** , President Trump’s lawyer and legal advisor, and one of the nation’s leading constitutional experts.
**Delegates are responding to a proven fighter who knows how to get results** , with two major courtroom wins against Dana Nessel ([dismissing the charges against President Trump’s alternate electors](https://kevinformi.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=39782b0ca6b504d2faad7a196&id=d89ae94d7d&e=4b10910eed) and keeping tens of thousands of high school students in person during the COVID lockdowns).
**Delegates are responding to a proven fighter that speaks truth to power, as I’m the only AG candidate that:**
✅ [Warned a township board that data centers threaten local control](https://kevinformi.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=39782b0ca6b504d2faad7a196&id=b82ee8b821&e=4b10910eed) of our communities and will raise energy prices for citizens.
✅ [Looked the Michigan Board of Education in the eye](https://kevinformi.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=39782b0ca6b504d2faad7a196&id=13c48568bd&e=4b10910eed) and said forcing radical gender ideology on our children is illegal.
✅ [Committed to take action to stop sanctuary cities and policies](https://kevinformi.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=39782b0ca6b504d2faad7a196&id=6e5360fdea&e=4b10910eed) shielding illegal aliens from deportation.
**Our momentum and our wins continues with you tonight**. Only together can we change Michigan’s political landscape, implement a rule of law culture, and deliver law and order for Michigan families this November.
I’m excited and I know many of you are as well. **So let’s make Michigan ruby red again**.
---
[|
---](https://kevinformi.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=39782b0ca6b504d2faad7a196&id=e67ffca5cd&e=4b10910eed)
| | **Let’s Keep Winning for Michigan Families!**
Thank you for your continued support and commitment to making Michigan red again. I'm honored to earn your vote at convention — **together, we'll secure this nomination and win big in November.**
Very truly yours,Kevin Kijewski
Republican Candidate for Michigan Attorney General

body:
State approval to farm? Lawmakers debate new limits on seed and pest control
| | | | [](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
| | Hi friends,
Listen to today's Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.joinrmv.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.joinrmv.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.joinrmv.). Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏛️ **Under the Golden Dome...** Lawmakers are advancing bills critics say expand state control over farming and immigration enforcement. SB26-062 and SB26-065 would restrict pest-control tools and require third-party approval for certain treated seeds—moves opponents argue [increase costs and erode property rights](https://link.email.joinrmv.). Scrutiny is also mounting after Palantir announced it’s relocating to Florida, [citing Colorado’s AI law](https://link.email.joinrmv.), while SB26-005 (the Sue Anyone Bill) [cleared the Senate](https://link.email.joinrmv.), opening the door to lawsuits tied to civil immigration enforcement.
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Dr. Janak Joshi is [running for U.S. Senate](https://link.email.joinrmv.), centering his campaign on border enforcement, deregulation, fiscal restraint, and preserving the American Dream. In Denver, parents are [suing DPS over alleged TABOR violations](https://link.email.joinrmv.) tied to lease-financing structures, while residents pressed leaders for answers after CoreSite [skipped a town hall on its new data center](https://link.email.joinrmv.), raising concerns about pollution and water use.
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** President Trump’s [State of the Union](https://link.email.joinrmv.) focused on middle-class tax relief, energy costs, fraud prevention, and retirement reforms, declaring America “bigger, richer, and stronger.” A defining moment came when [Democrats remained seated](https://link.email.joinrmv.) as Republicans stood for prioritizing American citizens. Meanwhile, the [Senate failed to advance DHS funding](https://link.email.joinrmv.) amid a partisan clash over immigration enforcement, extending a partial shutdown.
This is your Mountain Minute for Thursday, February 26, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[State approval to farm? Lawmakers debate new limits on seed and pest control](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY SEN. BYRON PELTON, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
_Colorado’s farmers and ranchers already face significant challenges, including volatile commodity prices, rising input costs, labor shortages, and unpredictable weather. They should not also have to contend with a state legislature that increasingly seeks to regulate how they protect crops and livestock._
_Yet that is precisely what Senate Bills[26-062](https://link.email.joinrmv.) and [26-065](https://link.email.joinrmv.) represent: a top-down attack on agriculture that increases costs, undermines private property rights, and signals deep disrespect for the men and women who feed our nation and the world._
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
|
---
**[Running on the American Dream: Inside Joshi’s Senate Campaign](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **Janak Joshi enters GOP U.S. Senate race focused on restoring the American Dream:** The physician and former state lawmaker says he’s running to combat rising costs, protect opportunity for future generations, and counter what he views as failed Democratic leadership in Colorado and Washington.
* **Border enforcement and lawful immigration at the center of his platform:** Drawing on his own legal immigration story, Joshi argues the laws already exist but must be enforced, distinguishing clearly between illegal entry and immigrants who follow proper channels.
* **Smaller government, lower taxes, and fiscal discipline:** Joshi calls regulation “one of the biggest problems,” pledges to simplify government, cut fraud and abuse, and rein in federal spending to ease inflation and protect taxpayers.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
|
---

The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support!
[DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
|
---
**[Parents Accuse DPS of Sidestepping TABOR Limits and Violating Colorado Organized Crime Control Act](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** [DENVER GAZETTE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **Parents Allege Racketeering Scheme in DPS Financing:** A parent advocacy group has filed suit accusing Denver Public Schools of using a “shell corporation” and lease-financing structure to bypass voter approval and unlawfully mortgage school buildings, potentially violating the Colorado Organized Crime Control Act.
* **Bond Funds Allegedly Used to Cover Prior Debt:** The complaint claims DPS steered voter-approved bond money to retire older lease obligations and provide “general fund relief,” arguing voters were never clearly told bond dollars could be used to pay off non-voter-approved debt.
* **Long-Standing Structure Faces Unprecedented Legal Test:** While certificates of participation have been upheld in the past, challengers argue DPS’s structure goes further than courts have examined, potentially putting dozens of school buildings at risk if lease payments lapse.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
|
